turns.query: Walk me through the one-point DO calibration options for a field sonde.

relevant.evidence:
There are two procedures that can
be used for a one-point calibration:
• Procedure 1—Calibration in air (can be accom-
plished with air-calibration chamber or wet-towel
method)
• Procedure 2—Calibration in air-saturated water
(water bubbled with air)

Manufacturers uniformly recommend a 100-percent satu-
rated oxygen calibration of DO sensors regardless of whether
calibration in air (Procedure 1) or calibration in air-saturated
water (Procedure 2) is used.

Procedure 1—Calibration in Air
This procedure is commonly used to calibrate optical
DO instruments.

Variation of Procedure 1—Air Calibration with a Wet
Towel
For many multiparameter instruments, a 100-percent
humidity environment can be created by wrapping a wet
towel around the sensor guard and inserting it into a plastic
bag.

Procedure 2—Calibration with Air-Saturated Water
This procedure, in which the DO sensor or instrument
system is calibrated in water that is saturated with oxygen at a
known temperature and ambient atmospheric pressure
